title: Closest Pins to the Center
statement:
A map shows pins at integer points points[i] = [x, y], and the center of the map is (0, 0). Return the k pins that are closest to the center by straight-line (Euclidean) distance, √(x² + y²). All pins are at distinct points.

Any order is accepted. If several pins are tied at the cutoff distance, any of them may be chosen to make up the k, so more than one answer can be correct.

examples.why: Squared distances are 32, 37, 4 and 50. [-1, 6] looks closer if you add |x| + |y| (7 against 8), but straight-line distance ranks [4, 4] ahead.
[1, 1] is closest (2). [2, 0] and [0, -2] tie at 4, so [[1, 1], [0, -2]] is just as correct.
With k equal to the number of pins, every pin is returned.

hints: You can compare distances without the square root: x² + y² orders the pins the same way. Sorting by it solves the problem in O(n log n). Can you do better when k is small?
You only need to remember the k best pins seen so far. When a new pin arrives, which of those k is the one it might replace?
Keep a max-heap of size k keyed on squared distance. Push each pin; if the heap grows past k, pop the farthest. What remains is the answer.

explain.intuition:
First, drop the square root. Distances are never negative and √ only grows, so ranking by x² + y² gives the same order with exact integers. Sorting all pins by that value and taking the first k is already correct, in O(n log n).

The heap version does less work when k is small. Walk through the pins and keep the k closest seen so far. The one a newcomer might replace is the farthest of those k, so keep them in a max-heap by distance: push the new pin, and if the heap holds k + 1 pins, pop the farthest. This is the same "keep the top k" idea as a leaderboard, turned around: to keep the k smallest you evict from a max-heap. It also works when the pins arrive as a stream that does not fit in memory. In Python, store (-distance, x, y) so that heapq's min-heap acts as a max-heap.
steps: For each pin compute d = x² + y².
Push (d, pin) into a max-heap ordered by d.
If the heap now has more than k entries, pop the top: the farthest of the k + 1.
After all pins, the heap holds the k closest. Return their points in any order.
pitfalls: Ranking by |x| + |y| or by max(|x|, |y|). Example 1 is built so that |x| + |y| picks the wrong pin.
Using a min-heap of all n pins and popping k times. That is correct, but it is O(n + k log n) with O(n) memory, not the bounded-memory version.
Taking Math.sqrt and comparing floats. It is unnecessary and invites rounding trouble; squared integers are exact.

solutions.title: Sort by squared distance
solutions.idea: Sort all pins by x² + y² and return the first k.

solutions.title: Max-heap of the k closest so far
solutions.idea: Keep k pins in a max-heap keyed on squared distance. A new pin goes in; if there are k + 1, the farthest comes out.

followups: Can you get average O(n) time? (Quickselect on squared distance puts the k closest in the first k slots.)
Pins arrive one by one forever, and at any moment you may be asked for the current k closest. Which solution still works?
